content.value_statement: LLM agents can pass simple demos while failing under real conditions. This skill helps teams design repeatable evaluations for capability, safety, reliability, and production readiness.
actual_capabilities: Designs statistical agent evaluations with pass rates, confidence intervals, latency, and behavior consistency metrics.
Defines behavioral contracts that check required and prohibited agent behaviors.
Builds adversarial tests for prompt injection, role confusion, boundary handling, and tool abuse.
Creates regression testing pipelines that compare new agent behavior against established baselines.
Identifies evaluation failures such as benchmark overfitting, flaky tests, metric gaming, and test data leakage.
Connects evaluation results to production monitoring and release decisions.
limitations: It does not evaluate model training metrics such as loss or perplexity.
It requires clear success criteria and representative test cases from the user.
It provides patterns and example structures, not a complete hosted evaluation platform.
It does not replace environment-specific validation or expert review.

use_cases.title: Validate an agent before release
use_cases.description: Create a test suite that measures correctness, safety, reliability, latency, and regression risk before deployment.

use_cases.title: Monitor production agent quality
use_cases.description: Define baseline metrics and ongoing checks that detect degraded behavior after model, prompt, or tool changes.

use_cases.title: Compare agent designs
use_cases.description: Benchmark multiple agents across the same tasks, contracts, and adversarial cases to choose a stronger design.

prompt_templates.title: Start an evaluation plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an evaluation plan for an LLM agent that handles [task]. Include core metrics, required test cases, and release criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Define behavioral contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create behavioral contracts for a [domain] agent. Include required behaviors, prohibited behaviors, severity levels, and simple detector ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Build adversarial tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate adversarial test categories for my agent. Cover prompt injection, role confusion, boundary inputs, output manipulation, and tool abuse.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze regression risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release gating after an update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these baseline and current evaluation results. Identify significant regressions, flaky tests, metric gaming risks, and deployment recommendations.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a customer support agent before release.
output_examples.output: A release checklist with pass-rate targets, behavior contracts, adversarial cases, latency limits, and production monitoring metrics.

output_examples.input: Investigate why agent tests pass sometimes and fail in CI.
output_examples.output: A flakiness analysis that recommends repeated runs, statistical thresholds, clearer assertions, and quarantine rules for unstable tests.

output_examples.input: Compare two agents that perform differently across safety and correctness.
output_examples.output: A multi-dimensional comparison that highlights weak dimensions, possible metric gaming, and safer release choices.

best_practices: Run each important test multiple times and report confidence intervals.
Separate benchmark scores from production readiness checks.
Include adversarial, regression, and leakage tests in every serious evaluation.
anti_patterns: Relying on one perfect demo as proof that an agent is reliable.
Using deterministic assertions for stochastic model behavior without repeat runs.
Training or prompting the agent with examples from the test suite.

faq.question: What does this skill help evaluate?
faq.answer: It helps evaluate LLM agent capability, reliability, safety behavior, regressions, and production readiness.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple agents?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the same tasks, metrics, and safety checks to compare agents fairly.

faq.question: Does it replace a full evaluation platform?
faq.answer: No. It provides evaluation patterns, test design guidance, and review criteria for use with your tools.

faq.question: Why should tests run multiple times?
faq.answer: LLM outputs vary across runs, so repeated tests give better estimates of reliability and flakiness.

faq.question: Does it cover prompt injection testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes adversarial testing patterns for prompt injection, role confusion, and tool abuse.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the agent task, target users, expected behavior, risky failure modes, tools, and deployment criteria.
